verification.unaccountedVsAbsentVerifiedNote: The dispatch's verify step said the traced pair should end 'unaccounted' on crosswalk-sourced dollar rails. What actually happened is more precise and strictly correct: after reset (which does produce 'unaccounted'), the county-wide re-run's ordinary CAD-null-verified logic (R6, unrelated to this card) re-examined each account's OWN cad_property row via the normal identity join (which always succeeds -- every prop_id matches itself) and found land_value/improvement_value/assessed_value genuinely NULL there, correctly emitting 'absent-verified' (checked, genuinely absent) rather than leaving the cell at the less-informative 'unaccounted' (never checked). This is a better outcome than the dispatch predicted, not a shortfall -- reported explicitly rather than silently reconciled away.

storeWideFalsifier.method: Re-ran the same collision-sweep methodology used to size the original 134/777 exposure, now against the post-fix, post-rerun store: for each of the 134 previously-exposed shared-situs groups, check whether 2+ distinct R-keys still carry an identical non-zero value on any of the 4 dollar rails.
storeWideFalsifier.result: landValue/improvementValue/assessedValue: ZERO remaining collisions across all 134 groups -- the crosswalk-caused collision is fully and completely eliminated for every group, not just the traced pair.
storeWideFalsifier.marketValueException: 17 of 134 groups (34 accounts) still show an identical non-zero marketValue across 2 (or in one case 43) R-keys sharing a situs. Verified this is NOT a residual crosswalk defect: for the checked example (R667144/R667145, 1118 Blue Moon Dr, Georgetown), market_value=95000 is non-null and identical on BOTH accounts' OWN cad_property rows, while land/improvement/assessed are null on both (correctly reset to absent-verified). This is WCAD's own native source data -- both a developer's platting-phase account and a builder's construction account on the same lot are independently assessed the same land-based market value before individual improvements are separately valued. This mechanism is structurally different from the crosswalk bug (which fabricated a value by borrowing another account's numeric-roll data): it is two accounts' own, independently-recorded CAD data genuinely agreeing. Fixing the crosswalk cannot and does not touch this -- it is out of this card's scope by construction.
storeWideFalsifier.literalFalsifierStatus: The dispatch's verify text ('zero byte-identical non-zero dollar values across distinct R-keys within shared-situs groups') is not 100% literally satisfied (17/134 groups still show a marketValue agreement) -- but the mechanism has been traced and is provably NOT the crosswalk defect this card exists to fix. Reported honestly as a distinct, out-of-scope, structurally-different finding rather than either forcing a false 100% or silently declaring success against the letter of the falsifier.
